Q1 Revenue
Why is contract revenue higher than last quarter and than the budget?

Pier 9 Tech Center was at full framing crews all quarter and Alder Point moved into interior work. Rainier Commons and Weller Street started in the quarter. Revenue is the job schedule: costs to date against estimated total costs on every job. Subcontractor costs rose with the work, so payables and the retainage we hold back from subcontractors rose too.
Q2 Billings
Why did the job schedule move from billings ahead of revenue at June 30 to revenue ahead of billings at September 30?

Mostly Alder Point. Its estimate now includes pending change order PCO-14 for the MRI suite shielding redesign, $640,000, which we priced and submitted on August 28. The owner’s architect has reviewed the pricing and we expect the owner to sign it in November. We cannot bill it until it is signed.
Q3 Margins
Why is the gross margin lower than last quarter and the budget?

Tideflats Cold Storage. In August we found cracks in tilt-up wall panels and 14 panels are being recast, and our insulated metal panel supplier raised its price 9%. We revised the estimate at September 30 from $16,284,000 to $17,480,000. We have a backcharge claim against the panel precaster that we have not recorded. The job is still profitable. No other job’s estimate changed by more than a rounding amount.
Q4 Accrued wages
Why did accrued wages nearly double since June 30?
The September 30 accrual covers wages earned September 14 to 30, paid on October 2 and October 16. At June 30 the accrual covered only June 22 to 30.
Q5 Interest
How is interest on the Cinderbrook loans recorded?
Interest on both Cinderbrook loans is accrued monthly. The bank debits it on the first of the following month.
Q6 Cash and the line
Why is cash lower and the line of credit higher than at June 30?

We drew $1,200,000 on the line on August 14 to pay subcontractors on Pier 9 Tech Center while two owner payments were late. Receivables are up because September billings were larger and Juniper Ridge Partners’ September billing was still open at quarter end.
Q7 Related parties
Do you have any transactions with related parties?

The Juniper Ridge Partners job (J-2625), nine flex units, is built for Juniper Ridge Partners LLC, a commercial developer with the same owners as HGC, building flex industrial units on land it owns. It is billed on the same terms as other owners.
Q8 Accounting changes
Did any accounting policy or estimate method change in the quarter?
No. We use the same cost-to-cost method and the same change order policy as at June 30.
Q9 Subsequent events
Has anything happened since September 30 that could affect the statements?
On October 9 we drew another $500,000 on the line. Lakeside Clinic started in October and was first billed on October 30.
Q10 Claims and litigation
Are there any claims, disputes or lawsuits by or against the partnership?
Only our backcharge claim against the Tideflats panel precaster. No owner has made a claim against us.
Q11 Covenants
Was the partnership in compliance with the Cinderbrook covenants at September 30?
Yes. Our compliance certificate goes to the bank by November 14, 2026.
Q12 Fraud and going concern
Do you know of any fraud or suspected fraud, or any doubt about the partnership continuing as a going concern?
No to both.
